# Issue #47: flag parsing treats "off " as true

A setting written as `off ` with a trailing space ends up enabled. This showed up
when reading feature switches from the environment. Please fix the flag parsing.

The bug is clear: `parse_flag` claims to ignore surrounding whitespace, but it only lowercases — so `"off "` (trailing space) doesn't match `"off"` and evaluates to `True`. Also, whitespace-only text should raise `ValueError` per the docstring, but currently returns `True`. Fixing both:

arguments.old:
word = text.lower()
    if not word:
        raise ValueError("empty flag")
    return word not in _FALSE_WORDS
arguments.new:
word = text.strip().lower()
    if not word:
        raise ValueError("empty flag")
    return word not in _FALSE_WORDS

arguments.summary: Fixed the flag parsing bug in flags/parse.py where a value like "off " (trailing space) was treated as true. The `parse_flag` function only lowercased the input without stripping whitespace, so "off " didn't match the false-word "off" and fell through to `True`. Added `.strip()` to the normalization step (`text.strip().lower()`), which also makes whitespace-only input raise `ValueError("empty flag")` as the docstring promises. Verified with the existing test suite (all passing) and direct checks: `parse_flag("off ")` → False, `parse_flag(" OFF\t")` → False, `parse_flag("   ")` → ValueError, `parse_flags("on,,off ")` → [True, False].
